items.title: The Proxmox web shell is so good that I've basically stopped using SSH in my home lab
items.summary: When I first installed Proxmox, I used the web shell almost exclusively. It was convenient and required little configuration to access my home lab from all of my devices, and that was good enough for me. It was only later that I started leaning on SSH as I added more containers, but honestly, I kept yearning for the ease of use of the web shell, and I began to log in using it more frequently. It doesn’t replace SSH everywhere, and I’ll get to where it falls short, but for the day-to-day work of keeping a Proxmox box healthy, it’s become my default way in once again.

items.title: PicPeak: Self-Hosted Photo Galleries That Make Sharing Easy
items.summary: Photo libraries and photo galleries aren't quite the same thing. I might want somewhere to keep thousands of family photos, but that doesn't necessarily mean I want to give everyone access to the entire collection. Sometimes I just want to put together a nice album from a particular occasion, send somebody a link, and let them enjoy the pictures without dealing with another account or app. PicPeak is built for exactly that kind of sharing. It's an open-source, self-hosted photo and video gallery platform originally designed with photographers and their clients in mind.

items.title: Palworld studio still hopes to release the game on Switch 2 one day, despite being in a legal battle with Nintendo
items.summary: Palworld, the survival crafting game featuring adorable animals seemingly inspired by Pokémon, has been embroiled in a legal battle with Nintendo over what the company alleges is patent infringement. But although the lawsuit is ongoing, Palworld developer Pocketpair still says it's keen to bring the game to Switch 2.

items.title: Glendale City Council approves Project Eagle data center, natural gas power facility
items.summary: Glendale City Council has approved the annexation and rezoning for Project Eagle/Baccara, clearing a major hurdle for a proposed data center and natural gas power generation facility near Litchfield Road and Olive Avenue. The roughly 160-acre development includes three data center buildings on about 108 acres, a natural gas power generation facility on roughly 33 acres, and a future APS substation on approximately 12 acres. Project Eagle refers to the data center portion of the development, while Project Baccara refers to the natural gas generation facility, which is expected to include 18 gas turbines.

items.summary: Considering the cozy co-op survivalbox Aloft put forth its final early access content update this past August, it was easy to presume that its next development destination would be 1.0. Sure enough, Astrolabe has confirmed that it will make its full release sometime early n ext year — along with its launch to the PlayStation 5 console.

items.title: Fileship: Self-Hosted File Sharing With a Desktop Companion
items.summary: I've been using self-hosted applications long enough to appreciate the little conveniences that make a difference in everyday use. Screenshot uploading is one of them. I don't want to open a file manager every time I need to share an image. I'd rather capture what I need and have it uploaded to my own server without thinking much about it afterward. It's a relatively small part of working with computers, but when you're regularly documenting things or sharing screenshots with other people, those extra steps can become annoying.

items.title: Raspberry Pi Zero 3 W & Raspberry Pi 4 Model A Surface In Linux Kernel Patches
items.summary: It looks like a next-generation Raspberry Pi Zero is about to surface, the long-awaited Raspberry Pi Zero 3 W. And in an interesting twist in these times amid high PC component costs and supply chain constraints, a Raspberry Pi 4 Model A. Merged to the official Raspberry Pi Linux kernel tree are patches adding Device Tree files for a Raspberry Pi Zero 3 W as well as a Raspberry Pi 4 Model A. It's been five years since the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W was released with many wondering whether any successor would come, especially in more recent times with RAM pricing and supply chain bottlenecks.

items.title: No Man's Sky Forsaken update brings Seamless Warping, New Cockpits, Forsaken Traders and more
items.summary: Somehow, Hello Games keep on adding impressive new bits into their ageing space survival game, with the No Man's Sky Forsaken update out now. Yes, another big free update for the game that came out in 2016! Truly showing certain other developers how it's done. My favourite addition here is probably Seamless Warping, allowing you while in space to direct your ship to a nearby star directly, instead of having to go through the galaxy map. There's also now an iOS version out too. See more in the full patch notes.

items.summary: Thousands of new homes are coming to northwest Surprise, but some families say schools havent kept pace with the growth. Now, voters are being asked to weigh in on Proposition 421, a $71 million Dysart Unified School District bond that would, in part, fund construction of a new elementary school in northwest Surprise and purchase land for a future high school. items.title: FAA Shields Voluntary Safety Reports
items.summary: The FAA finalized an order Wednesday protecting certain voluntarily submitted aviation safety information from being publicly disclosed. The order, published Wednesday in the Federal Register, covers information provided through the U.S. Aviation Safety Team (USAST), a government-industry partnership that identifies safety risks across the National Airspace System. The designation follows a proposal issued in August 2025. Information Covered The protections extend to safety reports, risk assessments, meeting records and information about the implementation of recommended safety improvements.

items.title: Google opens Android development to third-party AI agents and unveils new Gemini APIs
items.summary: Google is opening up Android Studio to third-party AI agents. Through a new "Bring Your Own Agent" feature, the IDE now supports more than 40 coding agents, including Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex. Google says new terminal tools also help agents finish UI tasks 77 percent faster while using up to three times fewer tokens. Android development is becoming agent-centric too.

items.title: CentOS Founder Builds Linux-Compatible Rust Kernel with AI in Just 11 Days
items.summary: Gregory Kurtzer, founder of CentOS and Rocky Linux, has unveiled Ginux, an experimental operating system kernel written mainly in Rust and developed with AI assistance in 11 days. Unlike Linux distributions, Ginux uses an independent kernel designed to run existing Linux userspace applications without relying on the Linux kernel. The project was developed as an experiment in what Kurtzer calls Human-Directed Agentic Engineering, a methodology where a human developer defines architecture, requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria, while an AI coding agent handles implementation, testing, debugging, and revisions.

items.title: Part idle game, part automation game, Moon Sweepers exploits the sickness in me that adores both Satisfactory and Cookie Clicker
items.summary: When Edwin talked about Moon Sweepers yesterday he focused on the artisanal approach to space rock cleaning. Like the puritan he is, he wants to wipe away all the dust on the moon using a toothbrush. He says you should take pride in your work, stick one spacesuit-clad middle finger up to the machines and say 'Fuck off, robots. Let me show you my art!" as you get down on all fours and brush away moon dust. I've taken a different approach.

items.title: OpenAI's Astra becomes the main target for Chinese AI labs after Anthropic tightens its defenses
items.summary: Chinese AI labs are now mainly tapping OpenAI's most powerful model, GPT-6 Astra, instead of Anthropic's Claude. According to The Information, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI leaned heavily on Astra's outputs to train their latest models. People familiar with the matter say this includes Kimi K3.1 Pro and V4.1-Flash 1017. This kind of distillation only works if the labs get the models to reveal their hidden reasoning steps. OpenAI and Anthropic both ban that. Moonshot declined to comment, and DeepSeek didn't respond to a request for comment.

items.title: I cut my Claude token use in half by moving instructions out of the main session
items.summary: I use Claude all the time for troubleshooting my self-hosting setup. It's been an incredible tool for everything from reviewing Docker logs to building small apps and dashboards, but letting it loose on a project can just as easily burn through my tokens and usage allowance. It turns out the complexity of the task isn't always what burns through AI tokens. The way the LLM works, exploring files or loading instructions can also dictate your token burn rate.

items.title: Rocky Linux Creator Built a New "Not Linux" Kernel in 11 Days Using AI
items.summary: Gregory Kurtzer is no stranger to the Linux world. He created CentOS, and when Red Hat messed it up, he started Rocky Linux as the community replacement. He also co-founded CIQ, the company offering enterprise support around Rocky. His latest project has nothing to do with rebuilding another Linux distro, though. He has built an entirely new operating system kernel, and he didn't write most of the code himself. An AI agent did. Meet Ginux, Linux userspace without Linux underneath The project is called Ginux.

items.title: Ubuntu plans firmware HWE to prevent issues on older kernels
items.summary: Ubuntu is planning a new linux-firmware-hwe package, in an effort to reduce the risk of firmware updates for newer kernels causing problems for users running older ones. On Ubuntu long-term support (LTS) releases, you can stick with the standard (GA) kernel it was released with for the duration of its support period, or you can install the HWE update, which brings newer Linux kernel versions to existing Ubuntu LTS releases. Right now, both kernels share the same firmware package, which means firmware updates designed to work with HWE kernels can cause problems for users who stick with the GA kernel.

items.title: Subnautica 2 dev thinks early access teams should worry less about adding features that are "very ugly, incomplete, or prototype"
items.summary: Subnautica 2 creative director Anthony Gallegos has spoken about what Unknown Worlds have learned over their many years working in Steam early access, exhorting other devs to add new features "as soon as possible" and experiment with them right under the flared nostrils of players. Damn the torpedoes, etcetera. The original Subnautica is one of the oldest Steam early access success stories, launching in 2014 a month or so after the program went live. Many of the final version's better qualities, including the pivot to horror epitomised by the spectacle of a Reaper grabbing your submarine's face, reflect observation of players and streamers in the wilds.

items.title: Hundreds of new homes planned for northwest Surprise as residents raise concerns about growth
items.summary: Hundreds of new homes could soon reshape another part of northwest Surprise after the City Council approved rezoning roughly 160 acres near Deer Valley Road and 231st Avenue. The land is now zoned for medium-density housing, with conceptual plans calling for more than 500 homes. Under military density guidelines for the area, the property could accommodate as many as 960 dwelling units. For some nearby residents, the project is another sign of how quickly their once-rural surroundings are changing.

items.title: Linux 7.4 Networking Brings Hardware Pacing Offload, New Drivers & More Performance
items.summary: The many Linux wired and wireless networking driver improvements were merged this week for the ongoing Linux 7.4 merge window.. New to the core networking code in Linux 7.4 is for hardware pacing offload functionality. This includes a new "pacing_offload" attribute for network devices. The IDPF driver is the initial one wiring up the support for pacing offload functionality that offloads to the NIC/SmartNIC the control of timing and spacing of outgoing network packets. Also in the core networking code are improvements to throughput for mixed BIG TCP / non-big TCP code paths yielding up to 70% throughput gains.

items.title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Jared Spiers
items.summary: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Jared Spiers had an interest in contributing to NASA’s mission long before becoming a civil servant for the agency. Growing up close to NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, and hearing about his father’s work there, he gained a firsthand connection to the nation’s space program. Before graduating high school, he knew exactly where he wanted to work. Spiers graduated from Pearl River Community College in 2017, where he earned three associate degrees in instrumentation, electronics, and electrical technology.

items.title: KSMBD Adds New Options With Linux 7.4
items.summary: A number of improvements to KSMBD, the in-kernel SMB3 file server, were merged for the Linux 7.4 kernel. A number of extended SMB2 directory information queries are now wired up for Linux 7.4. The new queries include FileIdExtdDirectoryInformation, FileId64ExtdDirectoryInformation, FileId64ExtdBothDirectoryInformation, FileIdAllExtdDirectoryInformation, and FileIdAllExtdBothDirectoryInformation. KSMBD also adds support for configurable per-connection session limits. There are also a number of POSIX improvements, validation enhancements, improved Windows chained-compression compatibility, improved encryption handling, and other security hardening enhancements.

items.title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and that's a problem for America's space agency
items.summary: For nearly a quarter of a century, Elon Musk and his essential partner at SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, viewed the United States government as El Dorado, the mythical city of gold. Like machete-wielding treasure hunters, Musk and Shotwell hacked through a tangled jungle filled with lurking carnivores such as Boeing and Lockheed Martin, as well as bean counters and regulators. Over time, against long odds, the pair cleared a path for SpaceX to contracts at NASA and the US military. They sued when things did not go their way.

items.title: Linux Kernel Developers Considering Removal Of KGDB Debugging Functionality
items.summary: Merged to the kernel all the way back in Linux 2.6.26 in 2008 was KGDB for improving the kernel debugging experience. KGDB works in conjunction with the GNU Debugger (GDB) to debug the kernel in a similar fashion to user-space debugging. KGDB requires the use of a second computer connected via serial or network cable. KGDB isn't widely used in recent years and a patch was floated today to remove it from the Linux kernel…

items.title: Graphics/NPU Driver Changes Already Begin Queuing Up For What Will Be Linux 7.5
items.summary: Since last week drm-misc-next pull requests have already been sent out to DRM-Next to begin staging new feature code for what's intended for the Linux 7.5 kernel cycle kicking off at the end of the year. items.title: Ghostty 1.4 is out with big improvements on Linux
items.summary: A major new release of Ghostty, the open-source terminal emulator, is out. Ghostty 1.4.0 brings a varied set of changes after seven months of development. There are welcome performance optimisations on Linux and macOS, a more capable SSH implementation and an easier way to rearrange tab splits – dragging them! This update to the Zig-based app offers complete Kitty graphics protocol support (including animation and relative placements) – the first terminal besides Kitty to do so. If you use TUI tools or script to render images in the terminal, this is a major feat.

items.title: Caltech Names Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman as NASA JPL Deputy
items.summary: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman has been named Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The emeritus astronaut and retired U.S. Navy captain begins his new role at NASA’s center of excellence for robotics and deep space exploration and at Caltech, which manages JPL for NASA, on Nov. 30, 2026. “Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

items.title: A Killer Hippo Horror Movie Is Officially Prime Video's Biggest Streaming Hit
items.summary: A low-budget horror movie about a killer hippo is currently the biggest streaming hit on all of Prime Video. "Hungry" is, on the surface, a little unassuming. It was given a blink-and-you'll-miss-it theatrical release earlier this year before making its way to VOD. It didn't have a major marketing campaign and has no A-list actors to speak of. According to FlixPatrol, writer/director James Nunn's "Hungry" is the number one movie on Prime Video, sitting above "Love of Your Life" and "Masterplan."

items.summary: A major project is moving forward after the Glendale City Council voted this week to annex land in Waddell to build a data center and energy plant. items.summary: nce the weather cools and thru-hikers leave, the Appalachian Trail becomes much quieter. While summer brings blooming mountain laurel and vibrant rhododendron thickets, the later season offers crisp autumn air and expansive ridgeline views through the bare trees. While higher-latitude and higher-elevation sections can face early winter conditions, the mid-Atlantic and southern AT truly shine during this time of year. items.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
items.summary: The private space tourism era looked so very promising five years ago. Blue Origin and Virgin Galactic had begun flying customers—real people with zero space experience—on suborbital missions. And at about the same time, private citizens were going to orbit for days at a time aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon. But that was then. Consider the state of play today: It has been 10 months since Blue Origin's New Shepard spacecraft flew its last mission in January. The program was subsequently "paused," but let's be real.

items.title: Astronomers Solve the Mystery of the Sun’s Spinning Plasma Jets
items.summary: The torrent of corona related discoveries keeps coming. Lately we’ve covered a variety of potential solutions to the “coronal heating problem” - why the Sun’s corona is so much hotter than its surface. Now, a paper led by a team of researchers from the University of Newcastle, Indian Institute for Astrophysics, and University of Sheffield, offers another answer - that we’ve been viewing the “spicules” that form in the lower solar atmosphere all wrong.

items.title: I stopped tossing old flash drives, and my homelab is better for it
items.summary: At one point in time, USB drives were all the rage for file transfers. I kept one in my pocket at almost all times and I had several around the house for various purposes. Over time, USB drives quietly stopped being so popular. But I still have uses for them in my homelab, so here are the main reasons why I’ll never throw away old USB drives.

items.title: Is Ubuntu Eyeing Immutability? Canonical Restarts Core Desktop and Eyes a Firmware Change for LTS
items.summary: Canonical has restarted development of Ubuntu Core Desktop, an immutable, snap-based take on Ubuntu that sat dormant after a developer preview in 2023. Jon Seager, Canonical's VP Engineering for Ubuntu, says a dedicated team is now working on it. The objective is for it to grow into the default Ubuntu desktop experience as the project matures. What you know of Ubuntu Desktop is not changing, and Jon says that the various Ubuntu flavors are under no pressure to build Core versions of their own. Separately, Juerg Haefliger, a Canonical engineer, has proposed a firmware package for Ubuntu LTS releases that would shield older kernels from firmware written for newer ones.

items.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
items.summary: United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company's 2026 launch schedule into oblivion. The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval.

items.title: NASA Welcomes Vietnam as Newest Artemis Accords Signatory

items.title: Crunchyroll to Stream Mashle: Magic and Muscles Season 3 Anime

items.title: Artemis III SLS Core Stage Joins Boosters at Kennedy
items.summary: NASA’s Artemis III SLS (Space Launch System) core stage is integrated alongside the twin solid rocket boosters on Oct. 28 inside the Vehicle Assembly Building’s High Bay 3 at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Technicians lifted the 212-foot rocket stage from the facility’s High Bay 2 using a one-of-a kind lifting beam designed to place the stage onto the mobile launcher. Once testing and checkouts are complete, teams will roll the core stage and booster stack out to Launch Pad 39B to conduct a tanking test where liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen fuel will be loaded only into the core stage and launch teams will practice countdown procedures and timelines.

items.title: Moon Habitats May Use Layered Mylar to Block Extreme Heat
items.summary: Living on the Moon, with either trained astronauts or regular civilians, could become a regular occurrence in the near future. However, it’s easier said than done, as scientists and engineers continue developing new and advanced ways for protecting humans in the harsh lunar environment, which contrasts the mild and habitable temperatures of the Earth. The most important aspect is focusing on keeping humans alive, and this includes temperature regulation within the habitats. However, how can you maintain temperature regulation while being flexible enough to withstand physical changes like moving, handling, and compression and expansion?

items.title: Stunning solar eclipse photos reveal giant hole and mysterious 'smoke rings' in the sun's atmosphere
items.summary: Newly released photographs of the sun captured during the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse reveal the sun's outer atmosphere in unprecedented detail. items.summary: United Launch Alliance said its fledgling Vulcan rocket would return to flight Friday, November 13, after a nine-month grounding due problems with its solid rocket boosters. items.title: NASA's New UV Space Telescope Will Launch in 2031
items.summary: NASA has committed to launching a new, more powerful UV space telescope. Named UVEX, the UltraViolet EXplorer, it will launch in 2031. It's about 100 times more powerful than its predecessor, GALEX, whose mission ended in 2013. UVEX will perform a survey in UV that will complement infrared surveys by other telescopes.

items.title: Retiring BSD-Compress Proposed For Linux PPP Network Code
items.summary: A patch has been proposed to remove the BSD-Compress support from the Linux kernel for the Linux networking point-to-point protocol (PPP) due to being unmaintained and having fundamental issues with the code that can lead to a fatal error. CONFIG_PPP_BSDCOMP allowed for BSD-Compress data compression for Point-To-Point Protocol connections. These days it's largely a legacy artifact. Linux developer Qingfang Deng laid out the case today for removing the BSD-Compress support from the PPP networking code due to a fatal error possible around the decoder's accumulator width on 64-bit systems leading to uncompressed packets.

items.title: Inside the Horror of Snook’s Arm: How Netflix’s ‘Below’ Brought Its Giant Cephalopod to Life
items.summary: Below is catnip for seaside horror fans. The show continues to thrive on Netflix, where its characters and mystery equally entertain. items.title: FAT32 File-System Seeing As Much As 265x Improvement With Linux 7.4
items.summary: A change merged for Linux 7.4 is showing some mighty big speed-ups for the FAT32 file-system. Open-source developer Matheus Alves de Almeida has worked through a patch affecting just a few lines of code that yield as much as a 265x improvement for FAT32. The change is adjusting the FAT driver's allocation code path with the status quo being to do many 1-cluster allocations when growing a file with FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE. The FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZEFALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE flag is used for pre-allocating disk space for a file but not changing the reported file-size.

Anthropic confirmed access to sales, HR, and IT data but disputes how deep the breach went. The incident shows how vulnerable even leading AI labs are through their external software dependencies.

But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters. items.title: EF-1 tornado confirmed northwest of Flagstaff, marking third in single day of Arizona storms
items.summary: An EF-1 tornado touched down near Wing Mountain in the Coconino National Forest on Wednesday, Oct. 21, the National Weather Service confirmed. items.title: Medieval Medicine’s Connection to Ancient Egyptian Mummies Revealed by New Study
items.summary: For centuries, medieval Europeans used material from ancient Egyptian mummies as medicine. Now, a new scientific study has uncovered chemical evidence that could help explain one of the more curious claims found in medieval medical texts: that Egyptian mummies contained aloe. Researchers at Marburg University in Germany have identified compounds associated with aloe in ancient Egyptian embalming material, potentially establishing a connection between mummification practices and medical knowledge transmitted through the Middle Ages.

items.title: AI often passes for human, but asking follow-up questions can trip it up
items.summary: Reading a conversation and deciding whether a chatbot wrote it can be surprisingly difficult. In a study involving more than 72,000 judgments of human and AI responses, participants frequently mistook machine-generated captions, word associations and conversational replies for human work. However, in a smaller experiment, direct questioning proved more successful at exposing a chatbot, though even that comes with caveats.

items.title: Wonderful Weather: Floods and Foreboding in 17th-Century Britain
items.summary: When the Bristol Channel flooded in 1607, it was not just one of the worst natural disasters in British history, it was also a sign, for many, that they had strayed from the path of God. items.title: A striking Mars cloud may be born from surprising physics
items.summary: One of Mars’ strangest clouds may rely on unusual physics to emerge. The Red Planet’s ribbonlike cloud — which stretches as long as four Grand Canyons laid end-to-end — may form without a speck of starting material to seed it, researchers report October 7 in Nature Geoscience. This manner of forming clouds, called homogenous nucleation, was thought to be possible on paper but not to occur naturally. Tiny particles such as dust or salt floating in the air seed typical clouds on Earth. But that cloud physics doesn’t seem to apply to the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud.

items.title: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning
items.summary: We introduce a sleep phase in continual learning, enabling large language models to continuously integrate new facts and enhance reasoning while mitigating catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs. Modern LLMs achieve impressive performance via pre-training and in-context learning (ICL). However, once deployed, they remain largely static, operating with a fixed knowledge cutoff date that leaves them unable to acquire long-term capabilities or adapt to new information.

items.title: Old Kingdom Tombs Investigated in Saqqara
items.summary: CAIRO, EGYPT— Ahram Online reports that a 4,000-year-old offering chapel belonging to Ikhetnefert, the wife of the high priest Sabu, has been discovered at his tomb in Saqqara by researchers from the Czech Institute of Egyptology. items.title: Solar + storage doesn’t automatically mean backup: Mapping what actually stays powered

items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
items.summary: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games. Tree Appreciator Emberwick Battle Drones Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun Cove Four times as insulting What happens if someone actually puts the work in?

items.title: OpenAI teases Dots for Europe, but its Berlin DevDay was really about building a platform
items.summary: At DevDay Exchange in Berlin, OpenAI mostly repeated what it had already announced, but it did share a few new details. The AI assistant Dots should roll out more widely in Europe "in a few weeks," and weekly Codex users in Germany have grown twentyfold since January. A clear subtext ran through the sessions and the repeated nods to ChatGPT's 1.2 billion weekly users: OpenAI wants developers to build their businesses directly on its infrastructure.

items.title: GDP report to give insight before Election Day. And, Israel's election is deadlocked
items.summary: As Election Day approaches, data suggest that the focus is now less on whether a Democratic wave will happen and more on its potential magnitude. Democrats continue to invest in competitive Republican-dominated races, and Republicans are matching those efforts. An NPR analysis found 70 districts where both Democrats and Republicans are investing more than six figures in their final messaging. These are the races to watch. Americans will receive a final reading on the country's gross domestic product and the state of inflation today before next week's midterm election.

items.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop ‘accelerating’ development ahead of 27.04
items.summary: Canonical has announced it’s ‘accelerating’ development of Ubuntu Core Desktop, its immutable, snap-based version of its desktop OS. Ubuntu Core Desktop was announced in 2023 and made available in preview for enthusiasts to try. But a lack of of obvious progress and direction (not to mention up-to-date builds) had left many wondering if Canonical was running cool on the idea. Now, things are finally kicking up a gear, says Jon Seager, VP of Engineering at Canonical.

items.title: Locals Sent Tesla FSD Down Bratislava’s Toughest Streets. It Needed Help
items.summary: Steep hills and tight gaps showed what FSD can do. Missed signs and driver takeovers showed how much supervision it still needs.

items.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
items.summary: Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu marginally ahead of his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but still short of a majority in parliament. With 93% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48. Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition.

items.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership across enterprise workflows
items.summary: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand their partnership to bring OpenAI models and agents into ServiceNow and ServiceNow workflows into ChatGPT and Codex.

items.title: Canonical Wants Ubuntu Core Desktop to Become the Future of Ubuntu
items.summary: Canonical has announced that development of Ubuntu Core Desktop, its immutable Snap-based Linux desktop, has officially resumed after the project was largely dormant following its 2023 developer preview. A newly assembled cross-functional team is now working to advance the project with the long-term goal of making Ubuntu Core the default Ubuntu Desktop experience. According to Jon Seager, Canonical’s VP of Engineering for Ubuntu, the project represents a fundamental change to Ubuntu’s desktop architecture.

items.title: New blood test can detect changes associated with Alzheimer's disease
items.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease can be detected by a new type of blood test — and a growing number of patients are asking their doctors about it. NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

items.title: Conan Exiles decides that it’s going to bring its Enhanced edition to consoles after all
items.summary: When Conan Exiles rolled out its fancy schmancy visual upgrades to its PC version earlier this year, console players felt the sting of being left in the gladiator pits with yesterday’s specs. Happily for the console crowd, Funcom decided that, yes, it’s going to be bringing Conan Exiles Enhanced to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series…

items.title: Even for Desperate Restaurants, Fake Reviews Just Aren’t Worth It
items.summary: When Yelp was first launched in 2004, it flopped. The company’s initial model of an email-based referral service failed to take off until its creators realized users were taking the platform into their own hands; in lieu of sending one another recommendations via email chain, they began using a “hidden” link at the bottom of the startup’s website to write unsolicited reviews of everything from doctors to restaurants. Yelp 2.0 launched in 2005, and gave those reviews a more visible place to live online — one that emboldened users to feel more authentic stewardship, by way of direct authorship, over hyping up the businesses they enjoyed (or didn’t).

items.title: Will rain spoil Halloween in Phoenix? Here’s the forecast
items.summary: Tricks and treats might not be the only things awaiting metro Phoenix residents over Halloween weekend. Rain is also likely, meaning you might possibly want to work an umbrella into your costume. The National Weather Service is currently forecasting an 80% chance of precipitation for the Phoenix area on Friday, with showers and possible thunderstorms bringing a wet start to Halloweekend. Storms on Oct. 30 could bring as much as three-quarters of an inch of rain to the Valley, including heavier downpours drenching some locations.

items.title: Fly fishing and fatherhood: The bonds built by water
items.summary: PHOENIX – In canals and streams across Arizona, an enticing commodity lurks below the surface, pursued by fly fishermen with eager but precise minds. But is it really the fish that they’re pursuing? For it’s been written with a romantic flourish that “many men go fishing all of their lives without knowing that it is not fish they are after” – a quote that is often attributed, probably incorrectly, to Thoreau. The answers vary, from the challenge and adrenaline that comes with a catch to the bonds built on the water.

items.title: FAA backs flight tests of JetZero’s top-mounted engines
items.summary: JetZero has been selected to receive $5.3 million under the fourth phase of the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) Continuous Lower Energy, Emissions and Noise (CLEEN) program, the company announced on October 28, 2026. The funding will pay for engine and nacelle instrumentation on Jet1, the full-scale blended-wing-body demonstrator the Long Beach, California-based company is building ahead of a first flight it has scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2027. Measuring airflow around top-mounted engines According to JetZero, the instrumentation will record airflow at the engine inlet and at the fan exit during takeoff, climb, cruise and crosswind ground operations.

items.title: Dems introduce new $15,000 EV tax credit bill that has no chance — and that’s a problem
items.summary: Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) wants to bring back the federal EV tax credit and double it. His new bill, the “21st Century Vehicle Choice Act” (H.R. 10881), would offer up to $15,000 on a new electric vehicle and $8,000 on a used one, and it would make both credits permanent. The problem is that the bill has virtually no chance of becoming law anytime soon. And if EV shoppers start holding out for it, it could end up hurting the market it’s trying to help. more…

items.title: Netflix Wins Bidding War for ‘AWOL’, a New Dramedy Series From the ‘Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves’ Duo
items.summary: John Francis Daley, Jonathan Goldstein, and Craig Rowin – mpetitive bidding war for AWOL, a new dramedy series from John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein’s GoldDay Productions, What’s on Netflix can confirm. It’s an early win for Netflix’s TV comedy slate, landing a project from one of Hollywood’s most in-demand filmmaking duos, and it adds yet another title to an increasingly packed list of upcoming Netflix comedy series. What is AWOL about? Story details are being kept firmly under wraps for now, with all we know being that AWOL is a dramedy.

items.title: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates
items.summary: The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%.The monthly increase was in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus.

items.title: Google debuts flagship Gemini 4 Carbon model with cybersecurity upgrades
items.summary: Google LLC today debuted Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier large language model adept at complex programming tasks. The LLM is rolling out just two weeks after the search introduced its previous flagship LLM, Gemini 4 Argon. According to Google, internal tests have shown Carbon to be more than twice as good at generating secure code.

items.title: More heat pumps would actually be good for the grid, researchers find
items.summary: Heat pumps, superefficient sources of electric heating and cooling, are winners for the climate, air quality, and typically a household’s energy bills. But a common claim cautioning against their widespread adoption in the U.S. is that the electrical grid is too strained to handle all the extra demand they would…

items.title: President of the European Central Bank Christine Lagarde to step down. Here's who is tipped to replace her
items.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down on Feb. 7 next year, she announced Thursday, formally kicking off a succession race that will be shaped by political bargaining and France's looming fiscal crisis. Lagarde has led the central bank since July 2019, steering its responses to the Covid-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and a series of energy price shocks that sent inflation in the European Union above 11% in 2022 and spurred the end of the post-Financial Crisis era of negative interest rates.

items.title: With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing well
items.summary: The U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI. Gross domestic product, which broadly measures economic activity, grew at an annual rate of 3.4% July through September, according to a report from the Commerce Department released Thursday. The previous quarter GDP grew at a 2.2% annual pace. A big driver for GDP growth in the third quarter was the strong investments from AI companies, which continue to build out data centers and spend big money in developing the technology.

items.title: these glowing amber sculptures begin with a natural polymer produced by tiny insects
items.summary: insects make the material for ori orisun merhav’s sculptures Brussels-based designer Ori Orisun Merhav is experimenting with a natural polymer produced by tiny lac insects, transforming their resinous secretions into glowing sculptures and sculptural furniture. Through her research practice Made by Insects, she heats and blows the amber-colored material into clusters of translucent bubbles, some perched on branching steel structures, others suspended as elaborate chandeliers. The material is known commercially as shellac, a substance typically used as a protective coating.

items.title: Jadens JD-166 Review: Portable, Inkless Thermal Printer on Linux
items.summary: For Linux veterans, printers can induce nightmares. Although, lately, printer support has vastly improved on Linux, at least for the newer models. Last week, I got my hands on Jadens JD-166, which is very different from all the printers I have used so far. It's a tiny device, almost a foot wide and only an inch tall and yet you can use A4 papers with it. There is no concept of ink here as it is a 'thermal printer'. Think of the last time you needed a printed agreement or a form while traveling, and had to hunt for a print shop.

items.title: Volkswagen’s EV battery recall reaches over 85,000, with Audi now included
items.summary: Volkswagen’s latest recall now extends to Audi, affecting nearly 13,000 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles globally. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity. Earlier this month, Volkswagen issued a recall with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) impacting 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs, model years 2023 to 2026. Official information from the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) revealed shortly after that several thousand more VW Group electric vehicles are affected worldwide.

items.title: LAUFEN unveils VITREON steel for contemporary washbasin designs
items.summary: VITREON STEEL EXPANDS LAUFEN’S ARCHITECTURAL UNIVERSE LAUFEN introduces VITREON steel, a new material that redefines the architectural possibilities of contemporary bathroom spaces. By uniting the strength and malleability of steel with the temper, chemical resistance, and non-porous gloss of glass, the material establishes a versatile new baseline for premium washbasins. The result is extraordinarily durable, scratch-resistant, color-fast, and fully protected against corrosion while maintaining a high standard of hygiene.

items.title: The 5 essential layers of AI agent sandboxing on Kubernetes
items.summary: An AI agent given autonomy to run code will inevitably run code no human has reviewed. It may install model-selected packages, run scripts generated moments earlier, and iterate until a developer’s test passes; that risk is limited to a laptop. For a company, it can extend beyond the agent’s workload to any workload deployed on shared Kubernetes infrastructure. Cluster configurations can limit a container’s system calls, but an allowed call that reaches a kernel vulnerability can still expose the underlying node.

items.title: Maricopa County sees higher-than-expected early voter turnout ahead of Election Day
items.summary: The Maricopa County elections website allows voters to search for the closest voting location, including drop box locations, or sort by shortest wait time.

items.title: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
items.summary: A fake medical emergency, an audacious jailbreak and a 36-hour search operation that ended with 17 prisoners being recaptured. Those are the highlights of a story from India's Tamil Nadu state that has captured headlines across the country. It began on Monday night after 17 men escaped from a prison in Theni district in the southern state after overpowering guards, and ended almost two days later with police catching them in batches. The incident has drawn attention to overcrowding in Indian prisons.

items.title: Europe has a weapon to wield against Chinese carmakers: its design history
items.summary: Walk around any city today and try to tell the cars apart. Go ahead, just try. They’re all smooth, rounded, anonymous blobs, shaped by the same wind tunnels and the same cost spreadsheets. But something is happening in Europe. The legacy automakers Renault and Citroën are rolling out more designs modeled after their most iconic silhouettes. At this month’s Paris Motor Show, Citroën unveiled an electric 2 CV Concept and a little delivery van to go with it, while Renault showed a reborn R8 Gordini and an E-Space concept to join the retro R5, R4, and Twingo it already sells.

items.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
items.summary: KYIV, Ukraine — Like many tech entrepreneurs in Ukraine, Yaroslav Azhnyuk turned to developing drone warfare after Russia's 2022 invasion. Drones have transformed the way wars are fought. Azhnyuk says artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. "When the other side has orders of magnitudes higher capabilities, it gives you an asymmetric advantage," he says. "It can make you 10,000 times more effective." Azhnyuk runs the Ukraine-based defense firms The Fourth Law and Odd Systems.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use
items.summary: It's almost like Google's got something to prove after taking a break from releasing new frontier AI models earlier this year. Just two weeks after rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon. This isn't the Flash model equivalent we've been waiting for but, rather, is an improvement on Argon, and like that model, Google is working on a staged release that could take a while. Stop me if you've heard this one before: Google says its latest AI model reaches a new threshold in coding, agentic tasks, and scientific analysis.

items.title: Alphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of search
items.summary: In Alphabet's across-the-board earnings miss, one segment stood out above all else: search. Revenue in the search and other segment grew 12% from a year ago to roughly $63 billion, but came in below estimates for the second straight quarter. At the same time, Google said search query growth on the platform was the strongest it's been in five years. The gap between usage and revenue within the search giant's flagship business is becoming harder to dismiss as more people turn to artificial intelligence bots and agents, including tools offered by Google.

items.title: Hegseth reportedly fires U.S. top military planner as Trump downplays Iran peace talks
items.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has reportedly fired the Pentagon's top military planner amid concerns that Washington may restart strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, according to the Associated Press. No reason was given for his dismissal, and nobody was named as his replacement. Sylvia has now retired, ABC News reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.

items.title: The 38 Best Restaurants in Barcelona, According to a Local Food Guide
items.summary: From Barcelona’s towering churches and bustling avenues to the sun-drenched beaches and idyllic plazas, it’s obvious why this city captures visitors’ hearts. You can also eat incredibly well here, and often for not very much money — though Barcelona loves a tasting menu and the World’s 50 Best Restaurant list awarded Disfrutar the No. 1 spot last year. Despite Barcelona’s famed cuisine, it’s also easy to have a downright disappointing meal if you settle for any old paella-slinging bar along Les Rambles (known in Spanish as La Rambla) or La Barceloneta.

items.title: Medieval ghost stories featured rotten flesh, the walking dead and spoon‑stealing spirits
items.summary: Stories of wandering spirits and the restless dead were common in the Middle Ages. These ghostly encounters were recorded in a wide variety of medieval literature.

items.title: robotic 3D printed regolith shells compose AENARA’s future mars habitat at powerhouse parramatta
items.summary: AENARA UNVEILS 1:1 MARS HABITAT AT POWERHOUSE PARRAMATTA Commissioned for Task Eternal at the newly opened Powerhouse Parramatta, Off-World Habitat Wall Section is a full-scale architectural installation designed by space architecture studio AENARA, founded by Melodie Yashar. Opening November 7th, 2026, the exhibition presents a physical cross-section of a conceptual Mars habitat envisioned for the year 2075.

items.title: Self hosting AI is too fragmented IMO
items.summary: I've been experimenting with running AI locally for a while now, and one thing that's consistently frustrated me is how many different tools you need depending on what you're trying to do. For stuff like LLMs, there's Ollama, LM Studio, Open WebUI, etc. For image generation, there's ComfyUI and other Stable Diffusion interfaces. Then you have separate setups for video generation, text-to-speech, transcription, music generation, and so on.

items.title: Data Center Health Worries Animate Midterm Campaigns
items.summary: PAGE, Ariz. — Doug Herrera still lives in the house his father built, though his dad died some time ago from cancer. Herrera wonders if that illness could have been linked to pollutants from nearby uranium mining. Now, he worries that a possible new neighbor — a proposed $10 billion mega data center — could imperil his health. “I’m a patriot, but I’m highly against the data center,” Herrera, 64, said from his front porch near a yard sign that reads “No Data Centers.” “There is light pollution, sound pollution.

items.title: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
items.summary: Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, as fighting intensified in the northern Tigray region neighbouring Eritrea. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is attending the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, described the acquisition as a "milestone" that would boost Ethiopia's defence capacity. He said Ethiopia and Russia agreed on the deal several years ago and the warplanes had come ahead of schedule. He also said that Ethiopia had plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow.

items.title: 3 more Linux-exclusive apps that are better than their Windows alternatives
items.summary: The usual narrative is that a Windows user switches to Linux and then complains about the app gap. That said, I’ve been using Linux for over 10 years, and when I switch back to Windows, I notice an app gap, too — in both functionality and quality. Now, I’ve already published a post covering Linux-exclusive apps that do a better job than their Windows counterparts, but there were enough left over to warrant a round two. So, here are three more apps that are only available on Linux and unlock a whole new dimension of computing that you've never experienced on Windows.

items.title: UV scans uncover natural varnish that may have preserved ancient Chauvet Cave drawings
items.summary: Tucked away inside a limestone cave in southeastern France lies some of the oldest artwork in existence. Known as Chauvet Cave, the site is so historically important—and fragile—that its location is kept secret and the cave is locked behind a huge steel door. And now, researchers have devised a technique to safely investigate these artworks and understand the natural varnish that has protected them for centuries. Their findings are published in the journal ACS Omega.

items.title: Arizona's 1st Congressional District now leans Democratic, two leading forecasters predict ahead of election
items.summary: Two leading political forecasters are now predicting that Arizona's 1st Congressional District is no longer a toss-up and is leaning Democratic. Sabato's Crystal Ball and the Cook Political Report now give Democrats an edge in the seat David Schweikert is leaving. Kyle Kondik, managing editor of Sabato's Crystal Ball, said the national mood is driving it. "In a year where Democrats are probably going to win the overall U.S. House race by half a dozen points or more, I think I'd rather be a Democrat in Arizona One right now," Kondik said.

items.title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
items.summary: Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users.

items.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
items.summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that people consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging. Six popular sweeteners were linked to faster cognitive decline, raising concerns about the long-term brain health effects of common sugar substitutes, although causation was not established.

items.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms
items.summary: Scientists have identified a weakened brain signal that may connect several seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity. The surprising discovery could help explain the disorder's underlying mechanisms and potentially lead to earlier detection and new treatments.

items.title: US economy grows faster than expected in report out just ahead of elections
items.summary: Growth is in sharp contrast to ​households’ assessment, reflected in ‌Trump’s record-low approval ratings The US economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter as resilient consumer spending and AI -driven ⁠business investment more than ⁠offset the impact ​of higher oil prices stemming from the conflict in the Middle East. Gross domestic product (GDP) increased at a 3.4% annualized rate last quarter, the commerce department’s ⁠bureau of economic analysis said in its advance estimate of the third quarter GDP on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast GDP advancing at a 3.2% pace.

items.title: NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
items.summary: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has discovered that Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind. The findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and could help scientists understand the enormous shock waves produced by exploding stars.

items.title: Nearly half of severely distressed generative AI users turn to chatbots for emotional support, study finds
items.summary: A new study has found that almost one in three Israeli adults surveyed who use generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools reported seeking emotional support, coping advice or mental health assistance from platforms such as ChatGPT and Gemini. Among users experiencing severe psychological distress, that figure rose to nearly one in two, according to researchers from Tel-Hai University of Kiryat Shmona in the Galilee and collaborating institutions.

items.title: Smaller ants devote more of their resting energy budget to their brains
items.summary: The energy required for brains of different sizes to function could play a role in how different species evolved over time. While the energetic costs of brains have long been deemed important in evolution, direct measurements of the rate at which the brains of different species consume energy, also known as brain metabolic rates (MRs), remain scarce.

items.title: Researchers identify critical window for boosting immunotherapy response in prostate cancer
items.summary: Researchers at Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center have shown that hormone-blocking therapies commonly used to treat prostate cancers temporarily activate the body's immune response before those immune effects begin to fade over time. In a new publication in the Journal for Immunotherapy of Cancer, a team led by Kent Nastiuk, Ph.D., reports this discovery—and points the way to a treatment strategy for taking advantage of this window of opportunity.

items.title: ​Pragmatic or pointless? Europe’s rift over whether to pick up the phone to Putin
items.summary: With no single European representative negotiating directly with Moscow, some leaders are establishing their own channels – with messy results The Nordic countries rarely fall out in public over foreign policy, least of all over Russia. But a 90-minute phone call this week to Vladimir Putin by the leaders of Finland and Norway drew an unusual rebuke from their Danish and Swedish neighbours.

items.title: Arizona's swing districts: What the final polls say one week before Election Day
items.summary: ARIZONA With Election Day one week away, the final polls are in and they show Democrats ahead up and down the Arizona ballot. Local pollster HighGround's final poll of the cycle has Gov. Katie Hobbs leading Andy Biggs by 12 points. The closest statewide race is Superintendent of Public Instruction, where Teresa Ruiz leads Kimberly Yee by 4 points. Pollster Paul Bentz says one group explains the Democratic advantage: independents. "Independents in particular have really rejected the Republican Party.

items.title: Why daylight saving time may be bad for your brain and health
items.summary: Turning the clocks back an hour each fall can feel like a gift: an extra hour of sleep. But the trade-off is less daylight in the evening, and the annual switch continues to earn mixed reviews. The same is true in spring, when we lose an hour as daylight saving time begins.

items.title: New World screwworm in Arizona dog; major storms forecast | Nightly Roundup
items.summary: From heavy rain threats later this week to a New World Screwworm case in Arizona, here's a look at your top stories tonight.

items.title: Did Medieval Merchants Invent Corporate Branding?
items.summary: Long before modern company logos became a familiar sight, medieval merchants were using distinctive symbols to identify their businesses, establish trust and build commercial reputations. A new study of hundreds of merchant marks reveals how these early forms of visual identity helped businesses operate across the Mediterranean. A study by researchers at the University of Barcelona has revealed how merchants in the late Middle Ages developed recognisable symbols that served some of the same purposes as modern corporate logos.

items.title: Why do flamingos dance while they eat? This scientist found out
items.summary: On a family trip to Atlanta, Víctor Ortega Jiménez spent time taking pictures and videos of flamingos as they fed in their pond. It wasn’t to admire their long legs or flamboyant pink color. Instead, he noticed the “beautiful” ripples spreading across the water as the birds ate under the surface. But he didn’t know why the waves were happening. It took “more than four years to answer that question,” says Ortega Jiménez, of the University of California, Berkeley. “But I think the answer was fascinating.”

items.title: Denisovan Fossils Identified
items.summary: BEIJING, CHINA— Phys.org reports that a new analysis of a skull fragment and jaw fragment found in northern China’s Xujiayao archaeological site in the 1970s suggests that the fossils belonged to Denisovans. Qiaomei Fu of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and her colleagues identified 18 proteins in the fossils. One of the collagen variants is found only in Denisovans, and not in Neanderthals nor modern humans. Then the researchers evaluated the shapes of the fossils and used 3D computer models to reconstruct the bones.

items.title: Why the Thirty Years’ War Redrew the Map of Europe Forever
items.summary: On May 23, 1618, Bohemian Protestant lords led by Count Thurn stormed Prague Castle, outraged that the royal Habsburg family wasn’t honoring the Letter of Majesty. Signed by Emperor Rudolf II in 1609, the letter had promised the Protestant estates of Bohemia freedom of religion and the right to build churches. During a heated confrontation at the palace, the lords threw two Catholic regents and their secretary out of a window. Although they fell from a height of roughly 70 feet, all three men survived.

items.title: Rare Roman Glass Re-created
items.summary: SHEFFIELD, ENGLAND—According to a statement released by the University of Sheffield, technician Lisa Hollands of the University of Sheffield has reproduced the color-changing effect observed in the Lycurgus Cup, a 1,600-year-old Roman glass cage cup that appears jade green in reflected light and ruby red when light is shown through it. The dichroic glass of the cup was cut and ground to produce an image of the mythical Thracian king Lycurgus ensnared in a vine. The Romans are thought to have produced the color-changing effect by adding small bits of gold and silver to the glass.

items.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
items.summary: URDA, Spain — Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network. Spain's network of high-speed rail has been considered one of the nation's crowning achievements. It ranks second to China in track mileage in the world. Until this year, it had not endured a deadly crash since coming into service over three decades ago. The collision Wednesday that turned a sleepy stretch of rail lined by olive groves into a scene of carnage came just four weeks before the country votes in a national election.

items.summary: Genie 4: our new world model unlocking unprecedented realism in real-time simulation.
