items.summary: See how Legora uses OpenAI models, ChatGPT, and Codex to accelerate legal workflows, expand contract analysis, and free lawyers to focus on higher-value work.

items.title: Crews can't rest despite record-low year for wildfires in Arizona
items.summary: 2026 has seen the lowest number of acres burned in Arizona in a quarter century, but there's still too much work to do and not enough resources in the high country.

items.title: How NATO Defeated Serbia in a 78-Day Air War
items.summary: The decision by NATO to bomb Serbia and Serbian armed forces in Kosovo was a symbol of NATO’s willingness to use military force to attain its goals. Having been accused of acting slowly in the face of prior Serb atrocities, NATO circumvented the United Nations and launched a ruthless bombing campaign, ultimately forcing Serbian forces to withdraw from Kosovo. The Geopolitical Spark in Kosovo In the 1990s, the former Yugoslavia was ripped apart by a series of brutal wars, including the Croatian and Slovenian wars of independence, and the Bosnian civil war.

items.title: Google just handed its rivals the keys to Android
items.summary: Google is giving coding agents like Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex deeper access to its Android development tools, including devices, performance profilers and production crash reports; now, agents can now investigate bugs, test changes, and verify their own fixes. The push spans Android Studio and the terminal-based Android CLI, with Google opening both to third-party agents rather than steering developers toward Gemini. Matthew McCullough, vice president of product for Android, has emphasized giving developers the freedom to choose their own models and coding agents.

items.title: Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers
items.summary: American automakers are reporting their third quarter earnings, and they're saying revenues are up, but they're also facing some serious headwinds. Or as Mike Wall, an analyst at the automotive data company Mobility Global, put it: If this year was a book about the auto industry, "It would be a mix of suspense and thrills and maybe a little bit of comedy and a little bit of horror." For the thrills: Auto companies are doing well when it comes to selling big cars and light-duty trucks. General Motors reported its sales of light-duty trucks rose 9% in the past year.

items.title: The New Wave of Sparkling Drinks Swap Zero-Sugar for a Shimmer of Sweetness
items.summary: For years, “zero sugar” has been the magic phrase in the soda and seltzer aisle. But while tasting for our inaugural Pantry Awards, we noticed a new crop of bubbly beverages making the case that a little sweetness might be a good thing. Recently, a torrent of sparkling drinks has flooded in-person and online shelves, all with a dash of sugar instead of zero or artificial sweetener. Some riff on seltzer water, others on soda pops, while some reinvent heritage libations, like switchel and agua fresca—all while tasting ridiculously refreshing.

items.title: The Ancient Bones Behind the Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos)
items.summary: Popularly known for its bright-colored decorations and ornamental sugar skulls, the Day of the Dead is among the most celebrated and highly anticipated holidays in Mexican culture. With origins in the Catholic All Saints’ Day, el Día de los Muertos is a celebration of the dead influenced by both Spanish culture, imported from Europe, and ancient Aztec customs dating back centuries. Today, Day of the Dead celebrations involve days-long festivals during which celebrants visit the graves of deceased ancestors and spend time with friends and family.

items.title: As No Man's Sky arrives on mobile, Hello Games celebrates with a spooky update for all that includes delivery missions and "seamless" interstellar travel
items.summary: Today's the day iPhone and iPad owners finally get to boldly go into No Man's Sky's procedurally generated universe, adding two more devices to the game's already long list of compatible platforms. But developer Hello Games isn't stopping there. It's also launching a new update, Forsaken, for all players, bringing a bit of seasonal spookiness to the exploratory space sim.

items.title: JetBrains Academy – October Digest
items.summary: Hello, October isn’t quite done yet! A few late arrivals made the cut, and they’re too good for us to hold back until November. Inside: A free frontend event about AI, a free way to practice reviewing agent-written code, our first Coursera specialization, and three full-stack Python courses. Events JetBrains AI.js Day 2026: Frontend’s scariest AI questions, live Frontend developers have some scary questions about AI, and on November 13, you can put them to experts live. JetBrains AI.js Day 2026 is a free online broadcast about the real tensions AI is raising, not the hype.

items.title: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.summary: Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act, which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations.

items.title: California Fire Department Orders Autonomous Firefighting Drones
items.summary: The San Bernardino County Fire Protection District has contracted with California-based Seneca to acquire five autonomous firefighting drones, according to an announcement Wednesday. The aircraft are expected to enter service in 2027 and would allow a single pilot to supervise multiple drones during wildfire suppression operations. The system includes five aircraft, a towable ground operations station and software designed to coordinate flights using onboard automation. Seneca claims the fleet can deliver more than 500 gallons of finished foam and respond to newly detected fires within five to 10 minutes.

items.title: Samsung stock slips despite posting its first-ever $80 billion quarterly profit
items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported third-quarter operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, making it the first tech company to exceed 100 trillion won in quarterly operating profit, the company said. That is equal to $80.04 billion, according to Reuters. Operating profit was 12.2 trillion won a year earlier. Revenue reached a record 195.3 trillion won, up 14% from the previous quarter. The Device Solutions division, which includes the Memory Business, posted operating profit of 106.5 trillion won on revenue of 147.1 trillion won.

items.title: Shell nearly doubled its profit and raised its stock buyback to $5 billion
items.summary: Shell $SHEL reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $10.8 billion on Thursday, up from $5.43 billion in the year-ago quarter, and announced a $5 billion stock buyback for the next three months. The buyback program is larger than the $3 billion repurchase Shell announced last quarter.

items.title: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.6% in September
items.summary: Monthly prices rose 0.5% in September, and core inflation reached 3.1% from a year earlier, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said…

items.title: The World's Newest Carnivorous Plant Is a Red Sundew That 'Death Hugs' Its Insect Prey. Its Survival Depends on a Rare and Disappearing Florida Habitat
items.summary: Florida botanist Lilly Anderson-Messec can quote the English poet John Donne by heart. “Any man’s death diminishes me, because I am involved in mankind. … Never send to know for whom the bell tolls; it tolls for thee.” Anderson-Messec stretches that oneness from humanity to ecology. She says a piece of her dies every time a native Florida plant goes extinct. “Whatever happens in this world happens to me,” she says. That perspective extends to a small carnivorous plant she first saw in 2014 while botanizing in the Florida Panhandle.

items.title: Economic growth accelerated over the summer, even as inflation stayed elevated
items.summary: Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second quarter and above the 3.1% forecast…

items.title: Best Espresso Machines for Coffee Nerds & Beginners (2026)
items.summary: Just a decade ago a homemade morning cup of joe in the US pretty exclusively meant drip coffee; The only people I knew with an at-home espresso machine were my friend’s very wealthy parents. Now it’s easier than ever to pull a double shot with a perfect layer of crema on top in the comfort of your own kitchen. Companies like Breville and De’Longhi offer whole slates of espresso makers, and high-end manufacturers like La Marzocco, famous for its commercial machines, have come out with home versions.

items.title: Found Object Masks by Romuald Hazoumè Counter Sorrow with Sympathy
items.summary: Tethered to the spiritual realm, blue connotes a sense of serenity and healing in Yoruba culture. It’s also the color of peace, and for Romuald Hazoumè, it’s an apt metaphor for considering the legacy of colonial violence, climate catastrophe, and the global crises transforming life today. In My Blue Period at October Gallery, the artist meditates on the contemporary geo-political landscape through a series of masks made from plastic jugs and found objects, like feathers, netting, and hardened paintbrushes.

items.title: These people are cutting the clutter and redesigning their smart TVs with AI
items.summary: On a quiet Monday evening, 42-year-old Igor Aguiar decided to give his 75-inch Amazon Fire TV a much-needed—and pointedly pious—facelift. Ninety minutes and a handful of AI prompts later, he sat back to admire his handiwork. The TV’s original home screen, once dotted with movie recommendations and toilet paper ads, was gone. In its place sat a sleek, colorful replacement launcher with shortcuts to his most-used apps and, more crucially, a breakdown of the day’s significance in the Catholic liturgical calendar.

items.title: Taiwan’s Biggest Airlines Return to Russian Skies After Pakistan Airspace Shock
items.summary: ISLAMABAD — Taiwan’s two largest international carriers, China Airlines (CI) and EVA Air (BR), have resumed flights through Russian airspace after avoiding it for more than four years. The route changes began on October 25, 2026, as the airlines adjusted services between Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) and European destinations following reports that Pakistan had restricted their access to its airspace under Beijing’s One China policy. The development highlights how geopolitical tensions can reshape international flight paths, even when airlines have not announced a formal change in their routing policies.

items.title: ‘Christmas at the Kringles’ Review – An Uneven Holiday Horror Tale with Nice Wrapping and Not Much Else
items.summary: This Halloween, Christmas comes early with Kevin Lewis ’ ( Willy’s Wonderland ) holiday horror-comedy, Christmas at the Kringles. But despite a talented cast of comedians, Lewis’ latest is a Santa’s sash filled with more coal than gifts. Neither all that funny, scary, nor even gory, it’s a film where the greatest horror is the reminder that some people take the holiday season a little too seriously. Penned by Zack Imbrogno ( Slayers ), the film stars Ron Livingston ( Office Space ) as Mark. His wife, Julie ( Rachel Bilson ), has convinced him to move back to the suburbs so their son, Bobby ( Jack Jewkes ), can have a more “magical” life.

items.title: ‘Alien: Isolation 2’ Takes Horror Outside With Smarter Adaptive Xenomorph And Brutal Weather System
items.summary: If the confined corridors of the Sevastopol space station provided claustrophobic chills and encounters in Alien: Isolation, the new planetary setting of the sequel, Alien: Isolation 2, will provide a very different experience in terror, according to the developer team. The sequel game is currently in development for PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and the Nintendo Switch 2, with the game taking place in the colony known as Kurasaki Station. In a Q&A video on YouTube, the dev team revealed more details about the Alien: Isolation 2 player experience, including new details on Blake, the game’s new protagonist, and how the new setting alters the horror experience.

items.title: Salle du Jeu de Paume in Versailles, France
items.summary: A few blocks from the lavish Palace of Versailles, hidden behind a small side street, you can find a commemoration of one of the most pivotal events in French history. Built so that the cream of the French nobility could have a place to play Jeu de Paume, a precursor to modern tennis, this large wooden room played a very minor role in the life of the nearby palace until the fateful year of 1789. That May, King Louis XVI called together delegates from across France to address the kingdom's economic crisis.

items.title: How Spiders Spin ‘Silk Dope’ Into Nature’s Toughest Material
items.summary: A spider, when knocked off a wall, doesn’t fall for long. Within milliseconds, it spins a soup of proteins into sturdy climbing gear. Using a thin, shimmering strand of silk, the spider hauls itself back up. The strand is tougher than Kevlar, the synthetic fiber in bike tires and bulletproof vests, and stronger than steel. It’s flexible and biocompatible with human bodies. Source…

items.title: One Nation accuses prime minister Anthony Albanese of trying to ‘exert undue political influence’ by offering David Farley an extra staffer
items.summary: Pauline Hanson says Anthony Albanese made ‘unsolicited’ offer of adviser with $200,000 salary to one of her MPs Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, offered the One Nation MP David Farley an additional staff member in what the party has called an “unsolicited” move, made in an attempt to win over the new politician using taxpayer funds. In a statement posted on social media, Pauline Hanson claimed the move, which would cost taxpayers as much as $200,000 in additional salary, was an attempt to “exert undue political influence” over politicians.

items.title: Crux Labs raises over $6M to improve enterprise agents with human judgment
items.summary: Crux Labs, an artificial intelligence platform turning enterprise judgment into continuous agent improvement, launched today with over $6 million in funding. Benchstrength and Misneach led the round, with participation from Analog Ventures and Pareto Holdings. The scale of enterprise AI agents in deployment can range from thousands to millions of user interactions per day. Existing observability…

items.title: Shell profits double to $10.8bn as Iran war pushes up margin on oil
items.summary: Energy firm to return $5bn to shareholders as climate campaigners criticise high profits Business live – latest updates Shell has doubled its profits in the last quarter after the Middle East conflict drove up the price of oil and gas and created shortages in the global market. Shell reported on Thursday morning that it made an adjusted profit of $10.8bn (£8.1bn) in the July-September quarter, up from $5.432bn in the third quarter of 2025. The results beat analyst expectations for a rise to $10.33bn.

items.title: Arden Point and Glenclyffe in Philipstown, New York
items.summary: Starting at the metro north Garrison train station, this hiking trail has various unique parts. During the first leg, you will find what appears to be an abandoned entrance to a building, in the form of a brick wall with door/window openings covered in vines and graffiti. Second leg you cross over a pedestrian bridge above the train tracks to Arden Point for various views of the Hudson River beyond. Third leg includes some bamboo forested areas as well as the path Benedict Arnold used to flee before his treasonous actions were discovered. There is signage and a display board with the history related to the historic Beverly Dock Road.

items.title: The Kitchen Gear That's Topped Our 'Best Of' Lists for a Decade
items.summary: A deluge of feature-laden, Wi-Fi connected, “revolutionary” new cooking products come out every year, yet there are some kitchen necessities that just can’t be improved upon. Believe us: At BA, we’ve been testing products head-to-head to find the best cookware, tools, and appliances since 2015, and during that decade, our editors have returned to a small handful of favorites time and again. With boxes full of kitchen gear arriving at the office practically every single day for our team of kitchen obsessives to put through the wringer, the odds are stacked against any particular item finding a stable spot as a favorite.

items.title: Polymathic AI and Princeton Researchers Release FlashMap, a Flow Map Drafter for 6.14x Faster LLM Decoding
items.summary: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton University, USC ISI, NYU and the Flatiron Institute have released FlashMap. FlashMap speculative decoding replaces the discrete diffusion drafter with a continuous flow map. It drafts a full 16-token block in 1 forward pass. Tokens in that block stay consistent with each other. On Qwen3-8B, the research team reports up to 6.14x lossless speedup on GSM8K. Drafter weights for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B are on Hugging Face, with vLLM and SGLang plugins. TL;DR Size: 0.5B-parameter drafter (500M for Qwen3-8B, 475M for Qwen3-4B); drafts blocks of K = 16 tokens.

items.title: World’s Tallest Barber Pole in Forest Grove, Oregon
items.summary: There’s something wonderfully absurd about pulling into a quiet Oregon park and finding a 73-foot barber pole just… standing there like it owns the place. I stopped by in May and couldn’t stop grinning. Forest Grove put it up back in the ’70s because some barbershop singers decided Texas’s “tallest” wasn’t tall enough. Classic Oregon energy. What makes it special isn’t the height or the stripes (though those red-white-and-blue bands still look sharp against the sky). It’s the pure, unapologetic small-town commitment to a joke that somehow became a landmark.

items.title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
items.summary: Who authorizes an agent’s actions, and how should teams manage growing context costs? The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee shares six session picks that tackle these questions, alongside open-source inference, agent standards, and audio AI. By Artenisa Chatziou…

items.title: Fighting rages near Yemen’s Taiz as UN urges humanitarian access
items.summary: Yemen Today TV reported on Thursday that fighting was taking place on the Al-Aqroudh and Al-Masrakh fronts, as well as in Al-Rahn village in the Sabir al-Mawadim district. Yemeni government forces in Taiz said they repelled attacks on Al-Aqroud, as they tried to break the Houthi siege of the area. “Our forces have carried out 749 military operations over the past 24 hours, resulting in the death or injury of 239 militants and the destruction of 117 vehicles and armoured vehicles,” Majid al-Nazili, a spokesman for Yemeni government forces, told Al Jazeera.

items.title: Gnome Hill in White Hall, Maryland
items.summary: Baltimore County's NCR Trail is a popular destination for running, walking, biking, and even tubing access. But it's also gnome to a unique and colorful landmark. Less than one mile north of the White Hall NCR Trail parking lot sits a small hill covered in gnomes, and gnome puns. The owner of the property estimates that Gnome Hill has been around for over 20 years, but says that it really gained momentum around 2020. Now, people frequently leave new figures for him to repair and add to the collection. While visiting, take a break on the courtesy bench and grab a drink or snack (cash only, honor system).

items.title: The phantom lighthouse: New research explains one of Australia's strangest illusions
items.summary: There are two lighthouses on Lady Elliot Island, at the southernmost tip of Australia's Great Barrier Reef. The first was built in 1873, but was decommissioned in 1995 when the second took over the job of warning ships off the reef. Visitors to the island, however, regularly report seeing signs of a third lighthouse. At night the beams of a nonexistent phantom lighthouse are seen far off, shining on the horizon.

items.title: Private equity is buying up more methadone clinics – access to the lifesaving drug isn’t getting easier
items.summary: Three times a week, Amber Titus wakes up at 5 a.m. to get ready for the 45-minute drive to the methadone clinic. Titus, 38, and her husband live with their two young children in Bisbee Junction, Arizona, a rural community near the U.S.-Mexico border. The couple started taking methadone, a medication that treats opioid addiction, in early 2025. “It’s been a godsend,” she said. But accessing methadone is not easy. The closest place they can receive treatment is a clinic in Sierra Vista, about 30 miles from their home.

items.title: Air Defense Systems Deployed Near Mar-a-Lago
items.summary: Ground-based air defense systems have been deployed around President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida, adding another layer of protection to the airspace surrounding the presidential retreat. The North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) and U.S. Northern Command confirmed the deployment in response to a request from the U.S. Secret Service. Officials have not said whether a specific threat prompted the move. The equipment, spotted near Donald J. Trump International Airport and aboard a barge in the Intracoastal Waterway, reportedly includes Avenger short-range air defense systems.

items.title: Detective Conan Anime's 4th Collection of Episodes 'Clash of the Red and Black' Streams on Crunchyroll, Netflix on November 1
items.summary: TMS began streaming the first specially curated selection of Detective Conan episodes in July 2025 on Netflix and Crunchyroll. The episodes are streaming in Japanese and with a new English dub by Studio Nano, different from the Bang Zoom! and Funimation dubs. The first selection of episodes is titled "Conan vs. The Black Organization" and features episodes with the titular antagonists, including ones that had never before been available in the U.S. Crunchyroll and Netflix added more episodes to the first collection in August 2025.

items.title: What we know of Vance’s letter to Rezaei, as Trump warns Gulf to ‘prepare’
items.summary: United States Vice President JD Vance has sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, in an 11th-hour push to restart peace talks, according to US media reports. The letter, which has reportedly been “received well” by Iran, aimed to gauge whether the US and Iran can narrow their differences enough to stave off a potential new round of US strikes on Iran, The Wall Street Journal has reported. The outreach comes as Trump warns the US’s Gulf allies to prepare themselves for a brief, high-intensity military campaign after next week’s US midterm elections, according to the Journal.

items.title: Ukraine: 13 killed in Russian drone strike on crowded Dnipro train station
items.summary: The death toll from a Russian drone attack on a passenger train which was stopped at a station in Dnipro in eastern Ukraine on Thursday morning has risen to 14, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed. According to Ukrainian state railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia, a jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform on which people were waiting to board a regional train to Zaporizhzhia, about a two-hour journey to the south. "Despite an increased threat warning, people were on the platform," the company said.

items.title: Zoology
items.summary: Description of the Lyon in Edward Topsell’s 1607 bestiary The History of Four-Footed Beasts: Lyons bones have no marrow in them and are so hard that they will strike fire. Their neck is made of one stiffe bone, without any vertebras. They have five claws on the hinder feet and the balls of their eyes are black. Lyons eat but once in two days, and drink in like manner. Formerly in England a Lyon could tell noble blood from base. There is a variety of Lyon with human faces. As for the rest, the taile of a Lyon is very long, which they shake oftentimes, and by beating their sides therewith they provoke themselves to fight.

items.title: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission 's publication on Monday of Anthropic's S-1 form —ahead of a heavily anticipated initial public offering—has led to plenty of discussion of whether the company's quickly ballooning revenues will be able to overcome its even higher costs. But amid the numbers and forward-looking optimism about AI "rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors, and the internet," Anthropic also spends an inordinate amount of time in its S-1 laying out the myriad risk factors that could bring the company down.

items.title: She Needed an EpiPen. But First, an Urgent Care Asked Her To Pay.
items.summary: Stephanie Rowell was standing on her parents’ front porch in July when a wasp stung her left arm. She said that almost immediately her arm felt like it was “on fire,” her body started itching all over, and her face became swollen and red. Rowell, 53, took Benadryl, and her father started driving her to the nearest emergency room, about 25 minutes away. But after driving for 10 minutes they spotted a TruHealthNow urgent care facility in Purcellville, Virginia, and decided to stop, hoping she would get help faster.

items.title: Pentagon says Iran war has cost US taxpayers $47bn: What that means
items.summary: The Pentagon has told lawmakers in the United States that the war on Iran has cost American taxpayers at least $47.1bn so far. The estimate, disclosed last week, comes just days before the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine if US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party will maintain control of Congress for the next two years. In a statement on Wednesday the Pentagon also said it had “successfully obligated 97.5 percent” of the funds Trump provided the department. Last July, Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) outlining tax and spending plans, which came into effect earlier this year.

items.title: Saharan dust carries desert bacteria across the Atlantic to Amazon rainforest
items.summary: Viewed under a microscope, the air above the Amazon rainforest teems with activity. It is full of pollen, fungal spores, tiny plant particles and bacteria. Normally, the composition of this bioaerosol community is quite stable. A team that included researchers from the University of Graz, the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz and Brazilian partner institutions has now shown that microorganisms are transported across the Atlantic along with desert dust from the Sahara.

items.title: A hidden ocean change near Antarctica could have global consequences
items.summary: The rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a dramatic shift in a crucial part of Earth’s climate system, scientists say. In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in a vast layer of the Southern Ocean, extending from 2,300 to 4,000 feet deep and encircling Antarctica. The shift reverses decades of freshening and echoes ocean changes usually associated with major global climate shifts over millennia but is now happening in just a few years.

items.title: Halloween 2026 Horror Guide: Where ‘Scream’, ‘Halloween’ & More Are Streaming Right Now
items.summary: Here's where to stream your favorite classic horror movies. Halloween is almost here, and there's no better time to turn off the lights, grab some popcorn, and settle in for a good old-fashioned horror movie marathon. Whether your idea of a perfect scary movie involves classic Hollywood monsters, haunted houses, bloodthirsty vampires, or masked killers, the streaming services have plenty of tricks and treats waiting for you.

items.title: Google Deepmind releases Gemini 4 Carbon just two weeks after Argon with gains across the board
items.summary: Just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, Google DeepMind is releasing Gemini 4 Carbon, which tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 with 59 points. Google says the model is built for extended agent workflows and the full cyber defense lifecycle. Because of those advanced security capabilities, access is limited to selected security experts at first.

items.title: I’m a Former Pastry Chef — I Tested HexClad’s New Bakeware, and I Totally Get the Hype
items.summary: Baking season is upon us, and that means we’re gearing up to make all kinds of Halloween treats, Thanksgiving pies, and holiday cookies. Whether you’re a practiced baker or a novice, one thing is true across the board: Exceptional baking requires a combination of precise technique and good equipment. Just like high-quality flour or vanilla extract can make a cake extra-special, so can a really great cake pan.

items.title: Airbus delivery slowdown squeezes profits, full-year target unchanged
items.summary: Airbus reported a decline in third-quarter profits, partly due to slower commercial aircraft deliveries; however, the planemaker left its full-year target unchanged. On October 28, 2026, Airbus delivered its nine-month and third quarter results, covering July to September 2026, when issues arose with both the A330neo and A321neo. Airbus’ EBIT Adjusted figures for Q3 fell 9% compared with the same period last year, dropping to €1.77 billion ($1.97 billion) from €1.9 billion ($2.1 billion).

items.title: Quoting Ted Sanders
items.summary: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement.

items.title: Microsoft profits soar days after announcing thousands of layoffs
items.summary: Technology giant Microsoft says its profits for the three months to the end of September jumped to more than $36.6bn (Â£27.5bn), just days after announcing plans to cut its workforce by more than a quarter. On Monday, the Windows developer said it would offer buyouts to around 60,000 of its workers to cut costs as it pours billions of dollars into artificial intelligence (AI). Like many other major tech firms, Microsoft is investing heavily in the infrastructure that powers AI even as questions remain over whether such huge spending will pay off.

items.title: Survey Finds Widespread Fatigue Among European Airline Pilots
items.summary: A new survey of 7,200 European airline pilots has raised concerns about fatigue management across the region, with nearly one-quarter of respondents saying they fly despite feeling too fatigued or unfit for duty. The European Cockpit Association (ECA) published the findings Oct. 27, drawing on an independent report by aviation safety consultancy Baines Simmons. The survey collected responses from pilots in 32 countries between Aug. 4 and Sept. 7, 2026, covering their experiences during the busy summer operating period.

items.title: Alfonso Cuarón’s Horror Series ‘Ascension’ Adds Amanda Plummer, Christopher Chung & T’Nia Miller
items.summary: The cast for Apple TV’s Ascension, the new cult horror series inspired by Adam Nevill ‘s novel Last Days, continues to grow. Deadline reports that Amanda Plummer ( Pulp Fiction, Needful Things ), Christopher Chung ( Slow Horses, Doctor Who), and T’Nia Miller ( The Haunting of Bly Manor, Generation Z) have joined as series regulars. They join previously announced Caitríona Balfe, who leads the cast and executive produces, and Bill Nighy. The series follows “a relentless documentary filmmaker and recently divorced mother, brilliant at uncovering others’ truths but struggling to resolve her own.

items.title: Ben Wheatley to Direct ‘Molepeople’ as LaKeith Stanfield and Rob Savage Exit Horror Film
items.summary: Despite being announced only earlier this month, LaKeith Stanfield has exited Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal’s Molepeople. Deadline reports that director Rob Savage, who’s been attached to the project since 2024, has also vacated Molepeople. Kill List and Normal filmmaker Ben Wheatley is now set to direct. Molepeople follows as a man descends into the abandoned tunnels beneath New York City, where he discovers a twisted society lurking beneath the streets. The film was slated for release in theaters worldwide on August 27, 2027, though there is no word at this time on whether this shakeup will create delays.

items.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
items.summary: Protein design tools may be getting increasingly sophisticated, but you still need a sophisticated understanding of protein structure for them to work. This can include knowing enzyme mechanisms down to the positions of specific amino acids, as well as the water molecules that also occupy the area where catalysis takes place. Once you specify these, the tools can build the rest of a protein around this target. A large collaboration of researchers based in China, however, decided to bring protein design to the masses, making a tool that can take natural language prompts and use them to produce proteins with the function you specify.

items.title: How brain implants turn thoughts into speech
items.summary: Casey Harrell lost his voice to ALS or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. As a volunteer in a clinical trial, he’s helping scientists test a brain-computer interface. Electrode arrays that are implanted in Casey’s brain send signals to nearby computers, where those signals are translated into words he intended to say. Casey uses this system every day to talk with his wife, daughter, friends and work colleagues. The moment he realized that it worked was “pure joy,” Casey says. Even though the researchers scripted his words for that first test, “it was a profound moment,” he says.

items.title: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
items.summary: Unproven but popular peptides touted for wellness have been available on the gray market, despite an official ban. Now, the Department of Health and Human Services is looking to bring them out of the shadows. HHS said in a new policy that it will exercise enforcement discretion for a half dozen peptides, essentially looking the other way when they're made by small compounding pharmacies. items.title: Playfully Vibrant Abstract Murals by Zebu Enliven Urban Walls
items.summary: For more than a decade, Berlin-based artists Lynn Lehmann and Dennis Gärtner, a.k.a. Zebu, have been transforming otherwise mundane walls and surfaces into vivid, geometric paintings. Moving between patterns and representational abstraction, the duo draw on their adjacent work in illustration and graphic design to create eye-popping compositions. Indeed, much of their practice is studio-based, so murals introduce broader possibilities in a variety of settings. “There’s something special about being able to interrupt someone’s everyday routine with an unexpected visual surprise,” the pair says.

items.title: Poundland's future hangs in the balance as chain edges towards collapse
items.summary: The future of Poundland hangs in the balance as the discount chain edges towards collapse, the BBC understands. The retailer's bosses filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which if approved by the High Court, will give the business 10 days breathing space to find a rescue deal. The move comes after Poundland's managing director Barry Williams wrote a memo to his 12,000 staff across its 600 stores in the UK and Ireland saying the chains' US owner had limited Poundland's access to funding.

items.title: Tom Hegen’s ‘The Mineral Age’ Documents the Indelible Effects of the Green Transition
items.summary: In its current form, the global transition away from fossil fuels will depend on the earth’s rare minerals. According to ClimateWorks, we’ll collectively need to mine 6.5 billion tons of cobalt, copper, lithium, nickel, and other materials before 2050 in order to keep up with energy demands. Most of these resources are found in regions already facing the greatest impacts of the climate crisis, from Chile’s Atacama Desert to Indonesia’s nickel reserves to the cobalt deposits of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

items.summary: Apple TV has always pioneered quality television, with every one of its original shows delivering strong characterization, deeply plotted stories, and the kind of cinematic-level of visual effects and cinematography that have become expected of streaming shows in recent years. items.title: Ted Raimi On New Screambox Talk Show ‘Your Dearest, Darkest Friend’: “Horror Fans Get It”
items.summary: Ted Raimi has worn many hats over decades of filmmaking. He’s an actor, a director, a writer, a producer, and an icon of multiple genres. Now, he’s trying on yet another hat, one that seems to fit him quite well: Talk show host. This week, Screambox will premiere Your Dearest, Darkest Friend, a funny, warm, in-depth interview series in which Raimi sits down with fellow genre icons ranging from actors to directors to musicians to talk about their creative processes, their careers, how they overcome adversity, and much more.

items.title: 3 Questions: Why infrastructure is entering a defining era
items.summary: For centuries, infrastructure has evolved alongside technology. New materials and engineering techniques enabled taller buildings, longer bridges, and larger cities. Computing and digital technologies later transformed how infrastructure was designed, monitored, and operated. Now, the pace of change is accelerating, and challenges are arriving simultaneously. Climate change is increasing pressure on water, energy, and other resources. Artificial intelligence is beginning to transform engineering and design, and its energy needs, along with aging grid infrastructure, is creating significant challenges, as well as new opportunities.

items.title: 2 college students found dead after going missing during Colorado hike
items.summary: Two Colorado college students have been found dead after going missing during a hiking trip in the Rocky Mountains last weekend when a heavy snowstorm hit, authorities said. The bodies of Kaden Matsuda, 19, of Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, of New York, were found Wednesday afternoon in a basin of West Apostle Mountain, about 100 miles (160 kilometers) southeast of Aspen, the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement posted on social media.

items.title: Navy Class A Aviation Mishaps Reach Decade High
items.summary: The U.S. Navy recorded 16 Class A aviation mishaps and 11 afloat mishaps in fiscal year 2026, according to data reported by USNI News on Oct. 27. Both totals were the highest in at least a decade, raising questions about the safety record across naval aviation and ship operations. The 16 aviation mishaps occurred between Oct. 1, 2025, and Sept. 30, 2026, and included manned and unmanned aircraft incidents as well as ground aviation mishaps. The Navy last recorded more aviation mishaps in fiscal 2014, when there were 17.

items.title: 5 Years Ago Today: Anya Taylor-Joy Starred In A Visually Stunning Horror Movie
items.summary: Filmmaker Edgar Wright's career arc leading up to "Last Night in Soho" — which debuted in theaters five years ago to the day — was interesting to witness. Starting in the late 1990s, he was a darling among Millennial nerds because he worked on "Spaced," the cult sitcom co-created by his frequent collaborator Simon Pegg. Wright then preceded to break out with 2004's "Shaun of the Dead," a film that seamlessly blends comedic zombie gore and 20-something anti-maturity malaise. From there, he directed 2007's "Hot Fuzz" and 2013's "The World's End" to round out his so-called Cornetto Trilogy, garnering even more acclaim.

items.title: Straw, Squeeze or Gravity? How to Choose the Right Water Filter for Your Adventure
items.summary: Portable water filters come in a lot of shapes and sizes, from ultralight straws you can tuck into a daypack to gravity systems capable of supplying water for an entire campsite. The good news: choosing one doesn’t have to be complicated. The right setup mostly comes down to how you plan to use it. A solo hiker stopping at streams along the trail has very different needs than a family filtering several liters for drinking, cooking and coffee at camp. So before comparing weights, capacities and technical specs, start with a simpler question: What will your adventure actually look like?

items.title: Air New Zealand Welcomes World’s First iMTOW Boeing 787-9

items.title: 1 in 4 Pennsylvanians say they paid out of pocket for their annual checkup. Why isn’t insurance covering these preventive visits?
items.summary: I was teaching health economics when a student raised his hand. We were discussing the Affordable Care Act, or ACA, which requires most health plans to cover certain recommended preventive services at no additional cost to patients. I explained that preventive care could cost nothing. The student had expected that, too. Instead, he said, he received a bill for more than US$500 after his checkup. He was so frustrated that he said he would never go back for another annual checkup. I suggested he contact his insurer to find out why he had been charged and whether his visit had been billed as preventive care.

items.title: Metroliner Trim Inspections Ordered After In-Flight Failures
items.summary: The FAA issued a new airworthiness directive Tuesday requiring inspections of pitch trim systems on certain Fairchild/Swearingen SA226 Metroliner and SA227 Merlin aircraft following reports of failures during flight. The directive, which takes effect Dec. 1, addresses concerns that moisture entering the trim actuators could cause them to malfunction and affect aircraft control. The FAA estimates that 198 U.S.-registered airplanes are affected. “The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in pitch trim actuator failure and reduced control of the airplane,” the FAA stated in the final rule.

items.title: ‘Hell chicken’ dinosaur likely dined on fruit, not meat
items.summary: Don’t let the name fool you: Infernogallus jamesi, aka the “hell chicken,” wasn’t some kind of ancient apex poultry. After extensively reviewing some of the most complete fossilized remains ever found of this Cretaceous era dinosaur, paleontologists now theorize the beaked species didn’t even enjoy meat at all. Instead, soft fruits were on the menu. The findings do more than simply repair the reputation of a turkey-sized dinosaur. In a study recently published in Nature Communications, researchers explained how I. jamesi and its evolutionary relatives paved the way for today’s fruit-loving birds.

items.title: The Silence Of The Lambs Achieved Something At The Oscars That Horror May Never Repeat

items.title: Can you understand your ballot? Many measures are written above a college level

items.title: Asia Pacific airlines end five-month passenger decline as cargo demand climbs
items.summary: International passenger numbers at Asia Pacific airlines rose slightly in September 2026, ending five consecutive months of year-on-year declines, while air cargo demand picked up pace. items.title: Aspen Airport Weighs Steep Landing Fee Increases for 2027
items.summary: Aspen/Pitkin County Airport in Colorado is considering a sharp increase in landing fees for 2027, with general aviation rates proposed to rise about 140% as the airport prepares to close for nearly eight months of runway reconstruction. The proposed rates would raise general aviation landing fees from $13.76 to $33.09 per 1,000 pounds of aircraft weight. Airlines operating under agreements with the airport would pay $31.84 per 1,000 pounds, up from $12.05, according to The Aspen Times. items.title: The Vibrant Color Wheels Designed by Goethe, Newton & Other Theorists of Color (1665–1810)
items.summary: Maybe it’s the cloistered headiness of Rene Descartes, or the rigorous austerity of Isaac Newton; maybe it’s all the leathern breeches, gray waistcoats, sallow faces, and powdered wigs… but we tend not to associate Enlightenment Europe with an explosion of color theory. Yet philosophers of the late 17th and 18th centuries were obsessed with light and sight. Descartes wrote a treatise on optics, as did Newton. Newton first described in his 1672 paper the “revolutionary new theory of light and colour,” the University of Cambridge Whipple Library writes, “in which he claimed that experiments with prisms proved that white light was comprised of light of seven distinct colours.”

As the 747 has transitioned from a passenger mainstay to a specialist cargo favorite, the market for its powerplants has split into two distinct tiers: the legacy engines for the 747-400 series and the cutting-edge units for the 747-8.

items.title: Revisiting Ecstatica - the pioneering survival horror that used its fancy ellipsoid graphics tech to fill its world with dongs
items.summary: There's a well-known phenomena in video games development known as time-to-penis. It's a somewhat tongue-in-cheek measurement of the time players, when given an exciting suite of new customisation tools, will take to create the first inevitable in-game dong. Ecstatica sort of implies it works the other way round too. That developers - when giddy with a new tech toy - can't always help themselves either. But maybe I'm getting a little ahead of myself.

items.title: Where to Stay When Visiting Alaska's Denali National Park
items.summary: The best hotels, lodges, and cabins for a trip to the Last Frontier. [#cneaudio: https://embed-audio.cnevids.com/script/narrated/8caaef97-05b6-4fbe-8d48-4f4ac4c3a7c7] With broad river valleys, colorful meadows peppered with fireweed and lupine, forests thick with spruce and aspen, and the snow-covered Alaska Range rising in the distance, Denali National Park and Preserve is one of those places that can still feel startlingly wild no matter how many times you visit. At 6.1 million acres, it’s larger than Massachusetts, and the sheer scale of the national park means a trip here can look very different depending on where you choose to stay.

items.title: United Airlines Adds 30 New Chef’s Table Dishes To Polaris Business Class From November 1
items.summary: United Airlines has revealed its next wave of Chef's Table seasonal dishes that passengers flying in its Polaris business class cabin will be able to enjoy from November 1 to December 31. The forthcoming rotation is the second full portfolio that United Airlines has rolled out as part of this initiative, following an initial summer launch on August 1. Notably, this will be the first-ever nonstop air link between Portugal and Central Florida.

items.title: NASA’s X-59 QueSST Heads to Kennedy Space Center
items.summary: On the anniversary of its first flight, NASA’s X-59 QueSST has started its first journey east from California, headed to the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. On Oct. 28, 2026, NASA’s experimental X-59 QueSST (Quiet SuperSonic Technology) celebrated a year since its first flight as part of the agency’s program which will pave the way for the return of supersonic airliners. On the same day, the aircraft departed for its first journey east from California. After a first stop in El Paso, Texas, the aircraft toward Fort Worth, Texas, where it landed at Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base (NAS JRB) Fort Worth for the night stop.

items.title: The Old-School Chicken Chain That You Can Only Eat At In These 13 States
items.summary: While there are many different styles of restaurants in the United States, those that specialize in chicken have become increasingly popular — according to Innowave Studio, chicken-focused chains are the fastest-growing fast food segment. While this is clear for nationwide chains like Chick-fil-A (which has a presence in all but two U.S. states), smaller shops have also experienced growth. Guthrie's Golden Fried Chicken Fingers, for example, has seen increased sales in recent years despite having a small footprint compared to its competitors.

items.summary: First announced back in March, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic: Community Edition is a fan-made mod (for Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, obvs) that spruces up Arkane's 2006 RPG, including upgrading it to a newer version of the Source engine. Details have been scarce since then, but an updated Steam page confirms what other additions the mod – which is being made with the blessing of both Valve and original publishers Ubisoft – is making.

items.title: A leaked trailer for Transformers: Reactivate shows off the only lick of gameplay we'll likely ever see of the cancelled co-op action game
items.summary: Back in 2022, Gears Tactics studio Splash Damage revealed that they were working on a Transformers game. It was called Transformers: Reactivate, and at the time was set to be a 1-4 player co-op action game, but come 2025 and the game gets canned all while parent company Tencent was going on a funding withdrawal spree in the games industry. Nothing substantial was ever really shown off of the game, but a trailer has now been leaked featuring what was apparently meant to be an internal look at it in action.

items.title: ‘They deserve our gratitude’: group rallies behind Arizona election workers
items.summary: Faith leaders and an Arizona Supreme Court justice gathered at the state Capitol a week away from the midterm election to call for the respectful treatment of election workers. Justice Maria Elena Cruz said she empathizes with election workers because, like judges, they endure vitriol from the public. She denounced the harassment of public servants and said Arizonans should appreciate the months of effort that goes into preparing for and carrying out an election. “When ballots are counted accurately and results are reported faithfully, the public rarely pauses to think about the thousands of careful hands that made it so,” she said.

items.title: San Francisco company offering $20 an hour to walk robot dogs
items.summary: A San Francisco tech startup posted a job listing offering $20 to dog walkers willing to spend four to six hours walking robot dogs.

items.summary: Dozens of demonstrators held a protest in front of Liberty Mutual's Boston headquarters to demand an end to the company's "Liberty Biberty" mascot.

items.title: ‘Crocodile Dundee’ Brought Me to Northern Australia. Aboriginal Guides Helped Me Understand It.
items.summary: At Anbangbang Billabong, a wetland in Kakadu National Park, our group was trying to find a specific tree from Crocodile Dundee. It appears in the scene where Mick Dundee switches from shaving with a razor to his large knife to impress American journalist Sue Charlton. The sandstone behind it was easily recognizable, but identifying a tree 40 years after filming was taking a little more effort. It was a good thing, then, that we were there with our guide, Mandy Muir, whose uncle was among the Aboriginal people consulted on the film.

items.title: "We basically rewrote the entire State of Decay game": Undead Labs spent years trying to make State of Decay 3 into a full-blown zombie apocalypse MMO
items.summary: State of Decay 3 was announced with a snazzy cinematic trailer all the way back in 2020. The open-world zombie game was due to move to colder climes, where you would face undead deer and survive the frigid elements. We've since learned that the teaser bore very little resemblance to what was actually being worked on, and was pushed out the door to plump up a Microsoft showcase. However, what the teaser also didn't reveal was that Undead Labs' ideas for the game were much larger in scope than the two survival games that came before. For several years they were trying to make State of Decay 3 into an MMO that captured the scale of a global zombie apocalypse.
